newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable as traders wait for direction.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable as traders wait for direction.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were little moved in quiet afternoon trading on Monday as most market players kept to the sidelines, unsure of market directions, traders said.
"U.S. was closed on Friday. So, basically there's uncertainty among traders as to what will happen when NYMEX opens tonight," one naphtha trader said.
The U.S. markets were closed for a national holiday on Friday.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half September was assessed at $199.00/200.00, compared with Friday's $199.50/200.25.
In the physical naphtha market, end-user activity remained slow with little storage space left for spot material.
High stockpiles at Japanese petrochemical manufacturers were mainly attributed to an increase in naphtha production by domestic refiners.
Japanese refiners' naphtha output totalled 1.3 million kilolitres in May, up 19 percent from a year earlier.

In low-sulphur waxy residue, Pertamina allocated 200,000 barrels of additional cargoes for July, traders said. They also said the Indonesian state-run firm may allocate another 100,000 barrels soon. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
